name: Mithredath
overview: Mithredath was a male figure known primarily for his role as the treasurer under King Cyrus, as recorded in Ezra 1:8. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided about him in Scripture. His position as treasurer indicates a trusted administrative role in the Persian empire during the time of the Jewish return from exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Mithredath means "gift to Mithra," reflecting a cultural background outside of Israelite tradition. This proper name is not given by God and is noted in Ezra 1:8. The meaning of his name does not carry theological significance within the biblical text but situates him within the broader Persian context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Mithredath beyond his role as treasurer of Cyrus. There are no listed relatives or connections in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mithredath is significant in the biblical narrative as an official in the Persian administration who played a part in the restoration of the Jewish people to their land. His role as treasurer under Cyrus would have involved managing resources and supporting the king's decree allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple. Thus, he represents the governmental authority cooperating with God's plan to restore His people.
